snippet.title: DAY 14/30 - INIESTA 2010 WORLD CUP REAL STORY 🙏
snippet.description:
Before the 2010 World Cup, Andrés Iniesta lost his closest friend. Dani Jarque — his teammate, his brother — died of a heart attack at just 26 years old. Iniesta carried that grief through the entire tournament.

Nobody outside his dressing room knew how broken he was inside.

July 11, 2010. Johannesburg. Spain vs Netherlands. World Cup Final. 0–0 after 90 minutes. Extra time. Spain had never won a World Cup in their entire history.

116th minute. Cesc Fàbregas slipped the ball through to Iniesta. One touch. Then a volley — low, precise, unstoppable. The net rippled.

Spain were World Champions.

Iniesta pulled up his shirt. Written underneath — "Dani Jarque, siempre con nosotros." Dani Jarque, always with us.

He had scored the most important goal in Spanish football history. And the first thing he thought of was his friend who never got to see it.

He stood there, alone in the middle of the pitch, crying — not just from joy, but from everything he had been carrying for months.

Some goals win trophies. That goal carried a soul.

snippet.title: CRISTIANO RONALDO OUT OF WORLD CUP AGAIN 💔
snippet.description:
Portugal 0-1 Spain. Dallas Stadium. July 6, 2026.

Stoppage time. Mikel Merino — a substitute — nipped into the box and fired past Diogo Costa. Spain through. Portugal out.
And Cristiano Ronaldo stood there on the pitch at 41 years old — the cameras finding him immediately — and the whole world knew what it was watching.
The last World Cup game of the greatest goalscorer in the history of football.

He had his chances. A shot from a tight angle saved by Unai Simón. Two efforts on target in a game where Portugal managed just 0.60 expected goals. Bernardo Silva's header off the bar in the dying seconds — the closest Portugal came. It wasn't enough.

6 World Cups. 144 international goals. 3 goals at this tournament. He equalised from the penalty spot against Croatia to send Portugal through. He gave everything.

But the World Cup — the one trophy that always escaped him — remained out of reach one last time.

Obrigado, CR7. 💙
